boulders.name: The Scarecrow
boulders.desc: A tall, gangly block standing alone at the end of the far field, arms out like a scarecrow.

boulders.name: The Tractor
boulders.desc: A boulder beside a rusted tractor nobody has moved since the farm closed.

boulders.name: The Haybale
boulders.desc: A round, squat boulder in the old hayfield, shaped like a bale of hay.

boulders.name: The Cow Pie
boulders.desc: A low, flat boulder in the old pasture. Watch where you put your pad.

boulders.name: The Milk Can
boulders.desc: A small, round boulder by the gate where the dairy left its milk cans.

boulders.name: The Salt Lick
boulders.desc: A tall boulder the dairy cows licked smooth, or so the story goes.

boulders.name: The Floodgate
boulders.desc: The big block beside the dam. In drought years you can see the drowned village's church steeple from its top.

boulders.name: The Retaining Wall
boulders.desc: A long, flat slab that looks almost poured, right below the dam's concrete wall.

boulders.name: The Buoy
boulders.desc: A round little boulder at the water's edge that floods every spring.

boulders.name: The Fossil
boulders.desc: A steep block with ancient ferns pressed into its shadowed underside, or so the locals swear.

boulders.name: The Wardrobe
boulders.desc: A tall, dark, boxy block deep in the ferns. Step under the overhang and it's always winter.

boulders.name: Mossback
boulders.desc: A boulder carpeted in moss that never quite dries. Bring a brush.

boulders.name: The Toadstool
boulders.desc: A tall boulder with a wide, overhanging cap, like a giant mushroom.

boulders.name: The Fiddlehead
boulders.desc: A rounded boulder among the ferns. In April the fiddleheads unfurl around its base.

boulders.name: The Hobbit Hole
boulders.desc: A low cave with a round opening, tucked into the gully bank. Cozy, until you try the V13.

boulders.name: The Sundew
boulders.desc: A steep block beside a boggy seep full of carnivorous plants.

boulders.name: The Lamp Post
boulders.desc: A tall, slim pillar standing alone in the ferns. Nobody knows who put the lantern on top.

boulders.name: The Stump
boulders.desc: A squat, flat-topped block beside an old-growth stump. One problem.

boulders.name: The Squeezebox
boulders.desc: A squat, steep box of granite in the hemlock shade, all squeezing and hugging.

boulders.name: The Snapping Turtle
boulders.desc: A low, domed boulder shaped like a turtle's shell. Its V13 bites.

boulders.name: Socrates
boulders.desc: A tall, thoughtful-looking boulder under the darkest hemlocks. Question everything, especially the beta.

boulders.name: The Hush
boulders.desc: A roof in the quietest corner of the park. People whisper here without knowing why.

boulders.name: The Owl
boulders.desc: A tall block in the hemlocks where a barred owl calls at dusk.

boulders.name: The Hearthstone
boulders.desc: A soot-blackened block beside a cellar hole, where a farmhouse chimney once stood. People say it's haunted.

boulders.name: The Stone Wall
boulders.desc: A slab cut by an old stone wall that wanders off into the woods, built by farmers who never met a rock they didn't stack.

boulders.name: The Barn
boulders.desc: A boulder with a roof like the sagging barn that once leaned against it.

boulders.name: The Root Cellar
boulders.desc: A low, dark boulder half-sunk into the hillside, cool even in August.

boulders.name: The Woodshed
boulders.desc: A short, steep block where the village kept its firewood. Something nasty lives here.

boulders.name: The Well
boulders.desc: A tall block beside a stone-lined well. Don't drop your chalk bag.

boulders.name: Gus's Rock
boulders.desc: The first boulder past the kiosk: a friendly slab where Ranger Gus finally put down his citation book and tried a problem.

boulders.name: The Tailpipe
boulders.desc: A low roof you climb lying on your back, like a mechanic sliding under a car.

boulders.name: The Cooler
boulders.desc: A flat-topped slab at tailgate height, the traditional spot for lunch and potato salad.

boulders.name: The Dumpster
boulders.desc: Squats next to the trash bins. Jugs, raccoons, and a faint smell of last week's pizza.

boulders.name: The Billboard
boulders.desc: A tall, blank slab facing the road, big and flat enough to rent out to advertisers.

boulders.name: Pickles' Rock
boulders.desc: A slopey overhang where Pickles, the lot dog, naps in the shade and steals unattended sandwiches.

boulders.name: The Tollbooth
boulders.desc: A small, technical slab right at the park entrance. Everyone stops here on the way in.

boulders.name: The Curb
boulders.desc: A knee-high lowball at the edge of the asphalt. Mind your ankles.

boulders.name: The Tombstone
boulders.desc: A tall, polished slab standing like an old headstone over the quarry waste.

boulders.name: The Headwall
boulders.desc: Part of the quarry's original cut face, still showing drill marks. Tall, technical, and right above the swimming hole.

boulders.name: The Stonecutters
boulders.desc: A block covered in practice chisel marks from the stonecutters who learned their trade here.

boulders.name: The Powder House
boulders.desc: A low, steep block beside the ruined shed where the quarry kept its blasting powder.

boulders.name: The Anvil
boulders.desc: A flat-topped, anvil-shaped block where the quarry blacksmith worked. Solid crimps on good rock.

boulders.name: The Monument
boulders.desc: A tall, squared-off block the quarrymen cut for a war memorial and never shipped. The best highball in the park.

boulders.name: The Derrick
boulders.desc: A tall block still wearing the iron eyebolts of the quarry's old derrick.

boulders.name: The Swimming Hole
boulders.desc: A steep block at the edge of the flooded quarry pit. Swimming is not allowed, which nobody believes.

boulders.name: The Rubble
boulders.desc: A heap of broken grout. Climbable, more or less.

boulders.name: The Offcut
boulders.desc: A neatly sawn slab of waste granite left over from the quarry.

boulders.name: The Reject
boulders.desc: A cracked block the quarry turned down. One problem, and not much of one.

boulders.name: Old Baldy
boulders.desc: The bald granite dome at the summit, where the hawk counters sit with binoculars every fall. Its traverse is the park's most famous problem.

boulders.name: The Thermal Slab
boulders.desc: A broad slab tilted to the sun, where warm air rises and hawks circle overhead.

boulders.name: The Lookout
boulders.desc: A tall block on the summit's edge with the best view in the park: the reservoir one way, the quarry the other.

boulders.name: The Aerie
boulders.desc: A tall, reachy block where eagles once nested. The hard lines are about flying.

boulders.name: The Birdhouse
boulders.desc: A boxy little overhang with a bird feeder nailed to the oak beside it.

boulders.name: The Raptor
boulders.desc: The tallest prow on the summit, leaning out over the trail like a bird about to strike.

boulders.name: The Weathervane
boulders.desc: A summit block under the rusted weathervane of a long-gone fire tower.

boulders.name: The Beak
boulders.desc: A pointed block with a sharp, hooked tip.

boulders.name: The Chickadee
boulders.desc: A tiny, cheerful boulder of easy problems, popular with beginners and chickadees.

boulders.name: The Perch
boulders.desc: A small, steep boulder where the hawks land. Short, but brutally powerful.

boulders.name: The Nest
boulders.desc: A round boulder with a bowl-shaped top full of pine needles.

boulders.name: The Engine Room
boulders.desc: The biggest cave at the old mill, stained with machine grease and crowded with eliminates. The mill burned here in 1891.

boulders.name: The Grotto
boulders.desc: A dripping cave lit by reflections off Mill Pond. Its hardest lines go deep into the dark.

boulders.name: The Millstone
boulders.desc: A round, worn boulder shaped like a giant grindstone, with slopers all the way around.

boulders.name: The Bullfrog
boulders.desc: A squat green boulder at the edge of Mill Pond. In spring the peepers are deafening.

boulders.name: The Waterwheel
boulders.desc: A boulder beside the old millrace, with the wheel's iron axle still sticking out of the stone.

boulders.name: The Doorstop
boulders.desc: A wedge-shaped slab that once propped open the mill door. Small, but the slab climbing is superb.

boulders.name: The Gymnasium
boulders.desc: A roof the size of a school gym, with enough holds for every link-up and eliminate imaginable.

boulders.name: The Belfry
boulders.desc: The tallest block at the old schoolhouse, where the bell tower stood. Crimpy, committing, and full of bats at dusk.

boulders.name: The Blackboard
boulders.desc: A tall, flat face of dark granite, smooth as slate, with crimps like chalk marks.

boulders.name: The Cafeteria
boulders.desc: A steep, juggy overhang where everyone gathers at lunchtime. Things get messy.

boulders.name: The Science Lab
boulders.desc: A steep, powerful block where the locals experiment with beta. Some experiments go wrong.

boulders.name: Detention
boulders.desc: A squat overhang behind the schoolhouse foundation, where the hard cases spend their afternoons.

boulders.name: The Sandbox
boulders.desc: A low, friendly rock in a patch of sand. The place to bring kids and first-timers.

boulders.name: The Apple
boulders.desc: A small, perfect boulder of rust-tinged granite. Only four problems, every one a gem.

boulders.name: The Lunchbox
boulders.desc: A compact little overhang packed with hard problems.

boulders.name: The Desk
boulders.desc: A small, flat-topped block carved with initials by a century of bored students.
